title: Prefetch Cost Controller: Key Design Guidelines and Safe TTL Apply Runbook
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: Deliver a pragmatic guide and implementation runbook for a cost-signal-driven prefetching controller and cache-key design constraints. Focus: hit-rate forecasting, TTL annealing strategy, prefix/key canonicalization heuristics, and automated safe-apply/rollback gates for production rollout.
background: We currently have heuristic TTLs and ad-hoc prefix keying in the runtime. Prior experiments show large variance in per-prefix hit rates when small changes to keying or TTL are applied. This work produces a repeatable simulation + staged rollout recipe so teams can reduce token cost while keeping 99th latency and output quality within SLOs.
goals: Define canonical keying rules for common pattern types (user prompts, system prompts, structured requests) to improve cache aggregation without over-collapsing semantics
Implement an offline hit-rate simulator that estimates delta cost and delta hit-rate for TTL and prefetch decisions with 95% CI
Design a TTL annealing algorithm that gradually reduces TTL per-prefix with conservatism knobs and automatic rollback triggers
Ship a safe-apply runbook: shadow dry-run, canary staged traffic, metric gates, and automated rollback orchestrator
proposal_steps: 1) Key design: create normalization ruleset that maps request metadata to canonical prefix keys. Rules expressed as prioritized regex/templating with example transformations.
2) Sampling harness: build a sampler that replays production traces (token-level) into an offline simulator to compute baseline hit curves by prefix and sequence length buckets.
3) Hit-rate model: use stratified bootstrap on samples to estimate p_hit(TTL) per prefix and compute expected token savings = (1 - p_hit) * avg_tokens * cost_per_token.

4) TTL annealing: propose TTL_new = max(1, floor(TTL_old * decay_factor)) applied incrementally over N steps. Decay defaults: 0.85 every step for low-traffic prefixes and 0.95 for high-traffic prefixes.
5) Safety gates: define metric thresholds to stop or rollback: hit-rate drop > 3% absolute OR cost reduction < 0.5% but latency 99th worsens by >5%.
6) Deployment: shadow mode (0% effect) -> 1% canary -> 10% canary -> full. At each step run A/B compare and require gate pass to proceed.
7) Observability: create dashboard widgets for per-prefix p95/p99 latency, p_hit, cost_per_prefix, and CI width on hit estimates.
8) Rollback automation: webhook-based rollback that triggers when gate metric exceeds threshold for two consecutive evaluation windows (5m windows).
risk_mitigation: Conservative default decay factors and minimum TTL floor to preserve functional correctness for stateful prompts
Shadow testing with full telemetry capture so we can detect subtle regressions before traffic is impacted
Per-prefix opt-out label to freeze critical customer prefixes during experiments
Manual override path and on-call playbook to revert changes while preserving rollout audit logs
acceptance_criteria: Automated simulator produces per-prefix p_hit(TTL) curves and a recommended TTL delta with 95% CI
A canary run (1% traffic) completes without gate violations for 24h and matches simulator prediction within its confidence interval
Runbook exists documenting exact commands, dashboards, and incident steps and is reviewed by SRE and Runtime leads
Rollback automation tested end-to-end in staging (simulated gate violations trigger revert)
